executive_summary.overall_assessment: The severity string-to-integer refactor is well-executed and the core pipeline is correct. The main gaps are: (1) changelog is incomplete, (2) a bool-as-int edge case in validation, (3) silent INFO fallback masks bad data in rendering, and (4) several skills duplicate content from the severity skill despite this PR introducing a no-redundancy rule.
executive_summary.summary_text: 22 raw findings from 3 agents, consolidated to 16 after dedup. No CRITICAL/HIGH. 5 MEDIUM findings need attention before merge. The severity migration itself is sound — issues are in edge cases and documentation consistency.
executive_summary.verdict_text: Merge after fixing changelog, bool validation, and applying the no-redundancy rule to the PR's own files.

findings.title: CHANGELOG 2.1.0 omits severity refactor and redundancy conventions
findings.description: The 2.1.0 entry only documents the release skill. Missing: severity integer migration, no-redundancy convention, backward compat removal.
findings.recommendation: Add Changed and Removed sections for the severity refactor and backward compat removal.

findings.title: Missing [2.0.0] comparison link in CHANGELOG.md
findings.description: The [2.0.0] entry has no reference link at the bottom of the file.

findings.title: Version bump may be incorrect — string severity removal is breaking
findings.description: Removing string severity acceptance is a breaking change for any tooling producing string values. Bumped as minor (2.1.0) but could warrant major.
findings.recommendation: Either bump to 3.0.0, or document that string severity was never a supported external contract and 2.1.0 is correct.

findings.title: check-pr-comments example shows schema_version 1.1.0 while referencing v2.0.0
check-pr-comments inlines severity mapping — violates no-redundancy rule
findings.description: Duplicates the numeric mapping that severity skill already provides. This PR introduces the no-redundancy rule but doesn't apply it to its own files.
findings.recommendation: Remove inline mapping, keep only 'See severity skill for definitions.'

findings.title: grumpy-review SKILL.md duplicates severity scale from severity skill
findings.recommendation: Simplify to 'severity (integer, per severity skill)' and remove the duplicated scale line.

findings.title: CDN Chart.js loaded without SRI hash (pre-existing)
findings.description: Chart.js from jsdelivr CDN has no integrity attribute. CDN compromise would allow XSS in triage page.
findings.recommendation: Pin version and add integrity/crossorigin attributes.

findings.title: Triage server pre-existing issues (unvalidated payload, 0.0.0.0 binding)
findings.description: Pre-existing: POST /api/decisions lacks schema validation; server allows network binding without auth. Not introduced by this PR.
findings.recommendation: Out of scope for this PR. Track separately.

findings.title: Python Code Quality
Boolean severity passes isinstance(int) validation
findings.description: Python bool is a subclass of int. severity=True (==1) passes validation and maps to INFO silently. severity=False (==0) is rejected by bounds check.
findings.recommendation: Add isinstance(severity, bool) check before the int check.

findings.title: sev_label() and compute_statistics silently map invalid severity to INFO
findings.description: SEV_LABELS.get(value, 'INFO') silently downgrades any out-of-range integer to INFO in both rendering and statistics. Masks data corruption.
findings.recommendation: Return 'UNKNOWN' or log a warning for values outside [1,5].

findings.title: SEV_LABELS and SEV_ORDER duplicated across two Python modules
findings.description: Identical definitions in both files. Change in one risks divergence from the other.
findings.recommendation: Extract to a shared module (e.g., scripts/severity.py).

findings.title: generate_remediation treats severity >= 6 as before_merge
findings.description: Condition 'sev >= 4' matches any value >= 4 including invalid ones like 99.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for float, None, and bool severity edge cases
findings.description: No tests for severity=3.0 (float), severity=None, or severity=True (bool).

findings.title: HTML severity filter relies on implicit string comparison
findings.description: JS filter compares dropdown string values against data-severity attribute. Works but fragile.
findings.recommendation: Use parseInt() on both sides for type-safe comparison.

findings.positives: The remediation bucketing logic is clean and readable after the refactor. Numeric comparisons are straightforward.
